test_title: SSC CPO 2025 Official Paper (Held On 11 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is the mandatory requirement of setting aside in liquid assets, such as gold or Government securities, by commercial banks?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Statutory liquidity ratio**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)** is a quantitative monetary policy tool used by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** that mandates **commercial banks** to maintain a specific proportion of their **Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL)** in the form of liquid assets.
 
• These liquid assets must be kept in the form of **gold**, **cash**, or **unencumbered government securities** (such as **Treasury Bills** and **Dated Securities**) before the bank can offer credit to its customers.
 
• The primary legal authority for SLR is derived from **Section 24 (2A)** of the **Banking Regulation Act, 1949**, which empowers the central bank to set and adjust this limit to ensure the **solvency** and **liquidity** of the banking system.
 
• By adjusting the **SLR**, the **RBI** can control the expansion of **bank credit**; an increase in **SLR** forces banks to invest more in **government securities**, thereby reducing the funds available for lending to the private sector and helping to curb **inflation**.
 
• Unlike the **Cash Reserve Ratio**, the assets under **SLR** are maintained by the banks themselves rather than being deposited with the **RBI**, and banks earn interest on the **securities** held under this requirement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)**:

 
 
• Refers to the share of **Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL)** that **commercial banks** are mandated to maintain with the **RBI** strictly in the form of **liquid cash**.
 
• The **RBI** does not pay any **interest** on the amount maintained as **CRR**, and it serves as a primary tool to regulate **liquidity** and **money supply** in the economy.
 
 
 
• **Current Ratio**:
 
 
• A **liquidity ratio** that measures a company's ability to pay its **short-term obligations** or those due within one year.
 
• It is calculated by dividing **current assets** by **current liabilities** and is a key indicator of **financial health** for non-banking corporations.
 
 
 
• **Margin Requirement**:
 
 
• A qualitative **monetary policy** instrument that refers to the difference between the **market value of collateral** offered for a loan and the actual **loan amount** sanctioned.
 
• By increasing the **margin ratio**, the **central bank** can discourage borrowing for speculative purposes in specific sectors of the economy.
